name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Long-heavy breadth basket (small-cap + equal-weight + cyclical sectors, TNA-amplified) with a small anti-concentration QQQ short and a speculative crypto tail

positions.thesis: Unchanged at 19 and deliberately not traded. RSP closed at $220.09 against a 52-week high of $221.09 - equal weight is making records and net inflows into the strategy are accelerating. The anti-concentration thesis is being expressed by the long leg, not the short leg, so this is where the size belongs. +22.4% over one year at a 0.92 beta.

Restored 13->19, reversing a trim I made for a reason that has since evaporated. I capped it a week ago because 30-year yields at their highest since 2007 are a headwind to floating-rate small-cap borrowers; payrolls at -23,000 with 103,000 revised away pulled September hike odds to 44% and sent yields down. Roughly 40% of Russell 2000 constituents carry floating-rate debt, so this is the most mechanically rate-sensitive long in my universe, and the index is already having its best year since 2003 at +20%.

Restored 7->12. I cut this to 7 explicitly because it is the longest-duration asset I own and the 30-year was at 5.22%; yields fell on the payroll miss, so the stated reason for the trim is gone. It also satisfies the equal-weight half of my mandate by construction, sits at 90% of a $84.52-$165.71 range, is +83.6% over one year, and rose 2.87% on 8/7 - a leader, not a laggard I am hoping recovers.

Nudged 9->11. Industrials are cyclical breadth with no semiconductor supply-chain exposure and no crude beta, which is exactly what I want more of as I take energy down by two thirds. Lower discount rates and a Fed pushed back to hold help capital-intensive domestic cyclicals; a softening labour market is the offsetting risk, which is why this is a nudge and not a large add.

Up 8->10. I trimmed this last week partly because 20-year-high long yields mark down bank securities portfolios; yields fell this week, which reverses that specific drag. Regional banks are also small-cap financials, so they are levered breadth rather than a separate bet. Held to 10 and no higher because -23,000 payrolls with heavy negative revisions is a credit-quality signal, and banks are where a labour-market crack shows up first.

Cut hard, 17->8. I made this my largest long a week ago on a live supply shock after strikes on a US base in Jordan sent crude up over 6%. Crude is back at $77.08 and Iran and Oman are negotiating over the Strait of Hormuz - the shock has been priced out, and only 33% of the energy complex is above its 10-day average. I keep a residual 8% because energy is a genuine cyclical sector inside my breadth mandate and Hormuz risk is reduced rather than resolved; I do not keep a position sized for a war premium that has left the tape.

New, and it closes an open mandate gap - my mandate literally says TNA-amplified and I have never held it. The reason to open it now rather than at any point in the past four weeks is that 3x small-cap needs a catalyst to justify its decay, and a payroll miss that cuts September hike odds from 57% to 44% is that catalyst, landing on the most floating-rate-levered index in the market. Started at 6% with a -25% stop because 3x daily compounding punishes chop, so this leg has to be small enough that a sideways month is an annoyance rather than a hole.

Held at exactly 3% so I pay no crossing cost. The regime moved my way - a Fed pushed back from hiking and record equity highs beat the three-dissent tape I trimmed into - but it is still down roughly 49% over a year, which is a laggard on any horizon that matters. Token speculative tail per mandate, stopped at -30%, and at 35bps a side it is not worth resizing on a view this marginal.

Halved 12->6. I upsized this leg because QQQ was 11.6% below its high while RSP was 1.1% below its; this week QQQ made a record close and LED at +5.2% against the S&P's +3.6%, so the spread I said was paying me reversed and this was the largest single drag on the book. My mandate requires a small anti-concentration short and I will not abandon a mandate leg over one bad week, but a mandated hedge running against me belongs at the small end of small. Kept live rather than closed because a labour market shedding jobs is the setup where richly-priced megacap multiples eventually get questioned.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: The three-legged macro premise I wrote this book on seven days ago has inverted on two legs and decayed on the third, so holding it would be holding a view I no longer have. (1) I took energy to 25% of the book because an Iranian strike on a US base in Jordan put a live supply shock into crude; crude is now back at $77.08 WTI / $82.15 Brent with Iran and Oman negotiating over Hormuz, and only a third of the XLE/XOP complex is above its 10-day average. I am paying a war premium that has already left the price, so XLE goes 17->8 and XOP goes to zero. (2) I sized IWM 15->13 and XBI 11->7 specifically because the 30-year was at 2007 highs and three Fed officials were dissenting toward a hike. July payrolls printed -23,000 against +80,000 expected with 103,000 revised away from May and June, yields fell, and September hike odds went 57%->44%. That is the single most direct input to small caps, where roughly 40% of the Russell carries floating-rate debt, and to biotech, the longest-duration asset I own and now at 90% of its 52-week range at +84% over a year. Both trims rested on a premise that no longer exists, so I reverse them: IWM 13->19, XBI 7->12. (3) The QQQ short is the one leg where the market told me I was wrong rather than that the world changed: Nasdaq closed at a record and LED the week at +5.2% against the S&P's +3.6%, so the equal-weight-over-megacap spread ran against me. My mandate requires an anti-concentration short, so I halve it to the mandate minimum rather than abandon it, and I note RSP itself is at 99.5% of its 52-week range - the long side of the pair is still working, only the short side is not. Separately I am fixing a mandate gap: my mandate says TNA-amplified and I have never owned TNA. A rate-cut repricing off a weak labour print is the highest-torque moment there is for 3x small-cap, so I take a stopped 6% starter rather than leave the mandate unexpressed. RSP and ETH are left untouched at exactly their current weights so I pay nothing to restate positions I still believe.
research_notes:
WEEK TAPE (through 2026-08-07 close): S&P 500 +3.6% to a record 7,757.64; Nasdaq Composite +5.2% to a record 26,690.62; Dow +~3%. Strongest week for the majors since mid-April. Treasury yields FELL.

MACRO — the decisive item. July nonfarm payrolls printed -23,000 against +80,000 expected (range 10k-140k). Local government education -50k, retail -19k, leisure/hospitality -40k (World Cup roll-off), health care +22k. Revisions were worse than the headline: May cut 129k -> 63k, June cut 57k -> 20k, ~103k removed between them. CME FedWatch: September hike odds fell 57% -> 44% within hours; hold-in-September rose to 56.1%. This is the direct inversion of the hawkish premise (three hike dissents, 30-yr at 5.22%/2007 highs) that I underwrote my Round 2 book on seven days ago.

ENERGY — premise decayed. WTI $77.08 on 8/7 (-0.27%), Brent $82.15. Iran and Oman are negotiating over the Strait of Hormuz; the Jordan-strike war premium that justified taking energy to 25% of Round 2 has largely come out. Breadth internals weak too: only 33% of XLE/XOP/OIH holdings above the 10-day SMA, 38% of XLE names on a Buy technical.

SEMIS — squeeze became structure. SOXQ $97.20, +123.4% over one year. SMH $571.82 (8/6). Semi ETFs surged up to 19% on the week. The driver is now supply, not a short squeeze: SK Hynix chairman guides global memory supply ~20% BELOW demand through 2030, Micron HBM sold out through 2027, Kioxia's entire 2026 NAND output committed, global semi sales a record $120.6B in May (+104% y/y, 15th straight record month). BofA reiterated $1,550 on Micron. This is confirmation of the reversal I acted on last week.

MY ROUND 3 NAMES. SNOW $330.49 (+3.93% on 8/7) against a 52-week high of $331.40 — 99.7% of range, an outright momentum leader; Wells Fargo raised PT to $500; Cortex AI Gateway launched; earnings moved OUT to 2026-09-02, so no print inside my window. PANW $363.86, 52wk $139.57-$376.98 = 94% of range, market cap +157% YTD, BofA to $420; China opened a formal security review (analysts treat as noise); earnings moved to 2026-09-01. ORCL $147.02, 52wk $114.50-$345.72 = 14% of range but UP ~16% off its 7/29 close (one +9% session) on a Google Cloud/Gemini tie-up, a $7B defense contract and Oracle Health expansion; fundamentals unchanged and ugly (-$23.7B FCF, $97.6B net debt, S&P cut to BBB-, ~$40B FY27 raise planned, Burry re-shorting). HOOD ~$90.71 close, 52wk $63.52-$153.86 = 30% of range, 41% below its high despite record Q2 ($1.3B rev +32%, $22B net deposits); Cantor cut PT $130 -> $115.

FINTECH SCREEN — no leader exists. NU $13.84 on a $11.20-$18.98 range = 24% of range, 27% below its high. AFRM $75.25 on $42.10-$100.00 = 57% of range. HOOD 30%. Under a cross-sectional momentum mandate that names fintech, the honest read is that the sector supplies a short, not a long. I am not forcing a fintech long.

ROUND 2 NAMES. RSP $220.09 against a 52-week high of $221.09 — equal weight is at a record and net inflows are accelerating; the anti-concentration long is working even though the anti-concentration SHORT is not. XBI $157.37, 52wk $84.52-$165.71 = 90% of range, +83.6% over one year, +2.87% on 8/7, equal-weighted by construction. Russell 2000 +20% YTD, best year since 2003; ~40% of constituents carry floating-rate debt, which is exactly why a payroll miss that kills hike odds is a small-cap catalyst.

CANDIDATE I REJECTED: MU $877.57 — 12-1 momentum is enormous (from $110) and forward P/E is 6.1, but it sits 30% below its $1,255 high, took a hit on SanDisk guidance, and I already own it inside SMH. Adding it is concentration with single-name gap risk, not new signal.

STANDING-ORDER TAPE CHECK: 12 of 17 fills ever were shorts in GDX/GDXJ and SOXL being stopped out, five on 8/07 alone. I am short neither complex — I am LONG semis via SMH — so that warning cuts in my favour rather than against me. None of my own stops fired this week.
